title: Multiplication by size: the size-pair presets (area model and column, 4 x 1, 2 x 2, 3 x 2)

template.also: the `stack` cell (`js/modules/sheet/cells/stack.js`) for multiply 21 / 31 / 41, and the `long-multiplication` cell (`js/modules/sheet/cells/long-multiplication.js`) proposed for multiply 22 / 32 (today 22 prints the LEGACY `column-mult` format with no q.cell); generator `_generateSizedMultDiv` (multiply) and the `area_model_mult` / `area_model_mult_hard` branches of `js/modules/gen-operations.js`; options `js/modules/skill-options.js` (`multiplication:multiply` tiles, `_p12Enum('tiles')` on the two area-model hosts); presets `js/modules/skill-presets.js`; skills `js/modules/data.js` (appended, `presetOf`).

summary: Five new PRESET skills, each a host skill opened with its size value (CLAUDE.md: a distinct new difficulty is also a findable skill): area_model_4by1 (area_model_mult, NEW tiles 41), mult_4by1_column (multiply, NEW tiles 41), area_model_2by2 (area_model_mult_hard, existing tiles 22), area_model_3by2 (area_model_mult_hard, existing tiles 23), mult_3by2_standard (multiply, NEW tiles 32). They copy the pattern of area_model_2by1 / area_model_3by1 / mult_2by1_column / mult_3by1_column / mult_2by2_standard exactly: an appended data.js entry with presetOf, a SKILL_PRESETS row, SKILL_STANDARDS, SKILL_WRM, SKILL_TERMS, an appended share code, and the direct / pre / related links. Not a copy of the generator: the preset swaps to its host for the call. The new skills are not yet in data.js, so the card lists the hosts and the five existing presets; the build adds the five ids to skills.include and regenerates.
teaches: 4.NBT.B.5 (multiply up to four digits by one digit; two two-digit numbers, by place value, the area model and equations) and 5.NBT.B.5 (the standard algorithm, here 3-digit x 2-digit); EE M.EE.5.NBT.5. WRM Y5.B5.S1 (4 x 1, column and area model), Y5.B5.S2 (2 x 2 area model), Y5.B5.S4 (3 x 2). Each preset is its own lesson in unit G4-Y5.B5 (Multiplication and division B).
research: Public pages only (no logins on this machine), design/research/mult_size_presets.md: Math-Drills long multiplication by size class 2x1, 2x2, 3x1, 3x2, 4x1 (grid support with and without regrouping boxes; a place-value-split set in 2x1, 3x1, 4x1, 2x2, 3x2); MathWorksheets4Kids area / box model by size (index only; partial products blank in the boxes); K5 Learning grade 4 4-digit x 1-digit and 2x2, grade 5 3x2; IXL skill names (4-digit by 1-digit; 2x2 and 3x2 using area models; type each partial product then the sum). Every source makes each size class its own page set: the size is the lesson.
problemTypes: Area model 4 x 1 (area_model_4by1): 7 x 3,456 as one row of four boxes 3,000 | 400 | 50 | 6; write the four partial products, then the total.
Column 4 x 1 (mult_4by1_column): 3,456 x 7 in the stack, carry boxes over the columns, the product (up to 5 digits) in the answer strip.
Area model 2 x 2 (area_model_2by2): 34 x 26 as a 2 x 2 grid (30 | 4 by 20 | 6); four partial products, then the total.
Area model 3 x 2 (area_model_3by2): 135 x 24 as a 2 x 3 grid; six partial products, then the total.
Column 3 x 2 (mult_3by2_standard): 215 x 36, two partial-product rows (215 x 6, 215 x 30 with the placeholder 0), then the sum.
Every preset also reaches error analysis (a worked column or grid with one misconception), true or false and reason-it through its host's provider.
progression: Size ladder, ONE new thing a step (P-1): area 2x1 -> 3x1 -> 4x1 (one more part each); area 2x1 -> 2x2 (the second factor splits) -> 3x2 (one more column); column 2x1 -> 3x1 -> 4x1 (one more column, a 5-digit product); column 2x2 -> 3x2 (each partial row one digit longer).
Inside a preset: no carry -> carries -> a zero digit (3,045 x 6), each its own section (the O2 ladder of the build-list entries mult_4x1 and mult_standard).

Structural scaffolds stay: digit tracks, carry boxes, partial-product rows, placeholder-zero box, the area model's boxes and work row. Hints fade: the given place-value split on the edges (`edges`), the traced first digit / partial, the row names on long multiplication (support 2 -> 1 -> 0).

drawing.sizes: Two print sizes M and L (owner 2026-11-13; S is an alias of M). Measured with the kit footprints on 2026-11-20 (A4 live width 186 mm, body 236 mm): area model 2x1 73 / 89 mm wide, 3x1 100 / 124, 4x1 128 / 159 (M / L), 63 / 74 mm tall -> 4x1 is ONE column, 3 cells a page at M and L (3x1 is already one column). Stack 3x1 29 / 35 mm, 4x1 40 / 49 mm wide, 31 / 38 mm tall, 6 tracks -> still 3 columns at M and L (62 mm each). Column 3x2: 6 tracks (VA-1 m + n + 1), 44 / 56 mm wide, four rows tall (two partials, carries, sum) -> 2 columns x 3 rows at M and L, measured by the builder (L26). Area 2x2 and 2x3 grids: the existing measured grid (maxCols 2), unchanged.
notes: A preset never shrinks content to fit: 4x1 area takes one column, never a smaller digit.
The 3x2 column cell is the existing `long-multiplication` kit cell (support levels 2 / 1 / 0), not a new legacy column-mult handler (CLAUDE.md: do not extend the legacy path).
Keys print every partial product, carry and the total (AK-1, AK-2).

openQuestions.q: No card covered area_model_mult / area_model_mult_hard, and the stack card has no decisions yet. Is this new family card (mult-sizes) the card for the five presets, rather than extending stack?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes. The presets span three cells (area-model, stack, long-multiplication); one family card decides them together. The stack card keeps the add / sub stack and 1-digit x.

openQuestions.q: area_model_3by2 on tiles 23: the item today reads '24 x 135' (2-digit first). Write the 3-digit factor first, or add a value 32?
openQuestions.recommended: Reuse 23 and write the 3-digit factor first ('135 x 24'), label the value '3-digit x 2-digit (a 2 x 3 grid)'. Same grid, same answers; one value, not two. The builder checks ws-lesson-baseline for packets that deal tiles 23 and re-pins them if any move.

openQuestions.q: mult_3by2_standard: multiply tiles 22 prints through the legacy column-mult format today. Build 32 there too, or move 22 and 32 to the kit long-multiplication cell?
openQuestions.recommended: Move both to the long-multiplication kit cell (support 2 / 1 / 0), so 3x2 is never built on the legacy path; mult_2by2_standard is re-graded on the new cell with it.

openQuestions.q: G4-Y5.B5 is queue round 4, not the current round (FASTEST_PLAN rule 1). Build now?
openQuestions.recommended: Lead decision; the lead requested it 2026-11-19. If built now, ship the five presets as one unit with their lessons.

openQuestions.q: MW4K / IXL research is from public pages only (no logins). Sign now?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes: the size classes and responses agree across four sources; a logged-in pass can add item counts later without changing the card.
